program_note:
This string quartet was written between June and September, 1989, and was revised in June and July, 1991. Each movement is a musical response to one of four Abstract Expressionist paintings: Dark Grey Tone on Maroon by Mark Rothko (1963), 1955-56-A (PH 1086) by Clyfford Still, Onement I by Barnett Newman (1948), and Blue Poles (No. 11, 1952) by Jackson Pollock.

I was intrigued to learn that in the early 1950’s, all four painters exhibited together at the Betty Parson’s Gallery, and occasionally congregated in her apartment for food and philosophy. The thought of these four seminal figures exchanging their occasionally similar but usually divergent artistic ideals suggested to me the idea of imagining how the artists would describe their works to each other through music.

It is hoped that the music will add to the paintings just as the paintings have added to the music.

Just as the artists in their meetings would not have spoken in any set order, so, too, the movements of this work can be played in any order. The order I have given is my preferred order, in part because the scordatura movement is separated from the other three, and because there is a real progression towards a climax at the end. Any order that the performers prefer, however, would be entirely acceptable.

Each explores a different aspect of counterpoint: Mark Rothko explores a very slow change of harmony, with almost no melodic motion. Clyfford Still is essentially one line that is “pulled” through the other instruments, leaving residual harmonies as it progresses. Barnett Newman develops one particular set of harmonies, until the whole explodes into an aleatoric uproar in which certain melodic fragments appear and disappear, until the whole subsides back into the harmonic stasis of the opening. Jackson Pollock introduces a melodic line in one instrument, and through the introduction of the other instruments, develops that melody into a dense — and then aleatoric — counterpoint with itself.

The total duration of the work is approximately 19:00, made up as follows: Mark Rothko: 5:00; Clyfford Still: 4:30; Barnett Newman: 6:15; Jackson Pollock: 3:15.

David S. Lefkowitz

25 July, 1991

Philadelphia, PA
